target.title: fix(worker): revalidate GitHub membership
target.body:
## Summary

- move GitHub org/team policy into a shared authorization module and revalidate signed user tokens against current membership on requests
- encrypt the OAuth credential inside version-3 user tokens, cache only successful membership checks for five minutes, and fail closed after cache expiry
- add immediate owner/login revocations plus a signature-only logout revocation path so a GitHub outage cannot strand active local Code viewer sessions
- document the re-login migration, cache controls, and narrow revocation mechanism

Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/902

## Verification

- `npm test --prefix worker` (815 passed, 1 opt-in live test skipped)
- `npm run format:check --prefix worker`
- `npm run lint --prefix worker`
- `npm run check --prefix worker`
- `npm run build --prefix worker`
- `node scripts/build-docs-site.mjs`
- focused org removal, GitHub outage, team removal, policy drift, owner/login revocation, centralized route denial, encrypted-token, cache, and logout-outage regressions
- autoreview: clean after fixing the logout/session-revocation finding

## Live proof

- injected the existing personal GitHub authorization only for the test process
- issued a version-3 Crabbox token containing the encrypted credential
- authenticated the exact local candidate through a real `https://api.github.com/user/memberships/orgs/openclaw` membership check
- received the expected owner/org/login authorization context; no credential value was logged or persisted

## Migration and secrets

- existing version-2 `cbxu_` tokens are intentionally rejected; users must log in again after deployment
- no new persistent credential is required: the existing GitHub OAuth access token is encrypted under a key separated from `CRABBOX_SESSION_SECRET` and carried only inside the signed user token
- optional `CRABBOX_GITHUB_REVOKED_USERS` and `CRABBOX_GITHUB_MEMBERSHIP_CACHE_SECONDS` are non-secret deployment controls
